root_cause.text: The Greybus BeaglePlay HDLC transmit path called `usleep_range()` from `hdlc_append()` while `tx_producer_lock` was held as a spinlock in `hdlc_tx_frames()`, causing a sleep-in-atomic-context bug when the circular buffer was full.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says `hdlc_append()` “calls usleep_range() to wait for circular buffer space, but it is called with tx_producer_lock (a spinlock) held via hdlc_tx_frames()”, and the patch removes that wait from `hdlc_append()`, adds `lockdep_assert_held(&bg->tx_producer_lock)` plus a `WARN_ON_ONCE` there, and moves the sleeping retry loop into `hdlc_tx_frames()` before `spin_lock(&bg->tx_producer_lock)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Tighten hdlc_append() into a lock-validated, single-byte buffer append helper and remove internal blocking/retry behavior by relying on the caller to precheck space.
intent_record.what: The function comment for hdlc_append() was changed to say it queues a single HDLC byte and to document that the caller must hold tx_producer_lock and ensure buffer space first. In the function body, the tail is now read once at the start, a lockdep_assert_held() was added, the previous retry loop with dev_warn() and usleep_range() was removed, and the function now performs a single space check with WARN_ON_ONCE() before writing the byte and advancing the circular buffer head with smp_store_release().
intent_record.how: At runtime, hdlc_append() no longer waits and retries when the transmit circular buffer is full; instead it assumes the caller has already reserved space and will only emit a warning and return if that contract is violated. This makes the function a strict one-byte append helper with clearer locking and ordering guarantees, and it avoids sleeping inside the helper.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix HDLC TX buffering so frames are only written atomically after enough space is available, avoiding partial enqueue and lock-sleep issues.
intent_record.what: Added a new helper, hdlc_encoded_length(), that computes the worst-case encoded size of an HDLC frame from a payload array, along with TX buffer wait constants. Updated hdlc_tx_frames() to calculate the required buffer space, wait and retry outside the producer spinlock until enough circular-buffer space is available, then recheck space under the lock before encoding. If space is still insufficient after retries or is lost before enqueueing, the function now logs a warning and drops the frame instead of partially writing it.
intent_record.how: At runtime, frame transmission now avoids sleeping while holding the spinlock and only enqueues a frame when the entire encoded HDLC packet can fit in the circular buffer. This prevents partial frame writes, reduces the risk of atomic-sleep issues, and makes overflow behavior fail safely by dropping frames when the TX buffer remains full.

grouping_result.intent: Fix HDLC TX buffering so frames are only written atomically after enough space is available, avoiding partial enqueue and lock-sleep issues.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix HDLC TX buffering so bytes are appended only when enough space is already available, removing internal blocking/retry behavior and preventing partial writes.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the root cause by removing blocking/retry behavior from hdlc_append() and requiring the caller to ensure sufficient buffer space before acquiring/using the spinlock, which prevents usleep_range() from being called while tx_producer_lock is held.

This retry loop keeps hdlc_append() blocking until space becomes available, which is the control flow that leads to the sleep while a spinlock is held.
